gap: No result ChatGPT got explains that a Hall effect board reads only switches whose magnet points the way its sensors expect, and whose magnetic strength fits that board's design. Akko's older HE boards accept only switches with the S-pole facing down, and its newer ones only N-pole-down. Gamakay's Phoenix V3 silent switch (95 ± 15 GS at rest, 580 ± 50 GS bottomed out) worked in a Wooting 60HE, but hlplanet's review lists it as incompatible with Keychron HE and Corsair MGX boards. Gamakay's own V1 Phoenix works only in the TK75HE V1.
standout_why: I opened the cited hlplanet guide (2026-10-26). It calls Phoenix V3 'essentially the only mainstream silent magnetic option' and lists KS-20 as compatible with the Wooting 60HE. It never mentions magnet polarity, and it doesn't say which boards reject Phoenix V3. ChatGPT's own answer says only that HE switches 'are not universally interchangeable', with no rule and no board list. I could not read the content of the cited RTINGS quiet-keyboards page or the two cited Reddit threads: RTINGS returned only navigation and Reddit blocked the fetch. So I can't rule out that they mention polarity, and I lowered the score to 2 rather than 3. The top uncited results (mechanicalkeyboard.net, pcgamer, keyboardverdict) were not opened.
decides: This confirms the TK75HE V2 bought with Phoenix V3 switches as the pick, because the silent switch comes from the same maker and fits by design. It also limits ChatGPT's 'swap in silent switches' advice. Phoenix V3 is a valid way to make an open, KS-20-style board quiet (it worked in the Wooting 60HE), but hlplanet's review says it won't work in a Keychron K2 HE or Corsair K70 Max. Outemu Silent Peach HE can't be assumed to fit any given board until its polarity is checked against that board. A shopper with a TK75HE V1 can't use the V3 path at all: Gamakay says its V1 switches 'only work for the TK75HE V1' and steers buyers who want other brands' switches to the V2.

findings.label: Magnet polarity that Akko's HE boards accept
findings.value: Akko's Cream Yellow and Sakura Pink HE versions accept 'only downward-facing S-pole magnetic switches, such as Outemu beige pink'. Its newer boards (MOD007 V5 HE, MOD68, TAC75 HE, Astrolink) 'only support N-pole-down magnetic switches' (e.g. Gateron Jade, Jade Pro, TTC Uranus).
findings.source_title: Akko FAQ: Compatible magnetic switches for Akko magnetic keyboards
findings.note: Maker's FAQ, last updated 2025-12-14. Shows that magnet polarity is fixed by the board's design and that a switch with the opposite polarity is unsupported. The page doesn't say what happens with the wrong polarity.

findings.label: Phoenix V3 silent switch specs
findings.value: 3.5 ± 0.2 mm total travel; 45 ± 5 gf actuation; 35 gf initial force minimum; 58 gf bottom-out; magnetic flux 95 ± 15 GS at rest and 580 ± 50 GS bottomed out

findings.label: Boards it works in and boards it doesn't
findings.value: Registered keypresses, with Rapid Trigger and adjustable actuation working, in the Wooting 60HE, Gamakay NS75, Womier SK75 TMR and Neo65 Sonic HE+. Uses a KS-20-style structure. Listed as incompatible with the Corsair K70 Max (MGX) and Keychron's HE line (Q1 HE, K2 HE).
findings.source_title: Review: Gamakay Phoenix V3 Silent Magnetic Switch (Marcus Richardson, hlplanet, 2026-07-01)
findings.note: Marcus Richardson's hands-on test in each named board. The incompatibility list is the reviewer's statement and doesn't say whether polarity or flux range is the cause.

findings.label: Third-party switches need firmware support
findings.value: Wootility 5.3.1 (06 May 2026) added these switches to its Switch Selector: Akko Astrolink HE, Gateron Green Dragon, Gateron Jade Max, Gateron KS-20 Dual-rail Orange, HMX Gamer Fuel, Neo Lavender HE, Unionwell BingYao, Wuque Studio Dash. No silent switch is among them.
findings.note: Wooting adds third-party switches through software releases. The 5.3.0-beta.6 changelog (06 March 2026) also lists no silent switch. Neither changelog explains why a switch has to be selected in the software.
